title: Visual Programming: Compositional visual reasoning without training
layout_note: Two stacked bordered examples (image editing on top, NLVR below). Each is a two-column table: a left column with the instruction or statement, the input image(s) and the final prediction; a right column with one row per program line, the step's intermediate output drawn at the left of the row and the code line at the right, joined by a short left-pointing arrow.
grouping: Each example is one black-bordered box; inside it thin rules divide the left summary column from the step table and separate the table into one row per program step.
shapes_depth: No boxes or modules at all: the figure is a table of real images (photos, black-background segmentation masks with labelled crops, edited images) and syntax-coloured monospace code; numbers and 'True' stand in for non-image outputs.
proposed_highlight: The method's product is the figure: each program step's intermediate result is shown as data next to the line that produced it; module names (Seg, Select, Replace, Vqa, Eval) are set in bold red in the code.
lesson: Show an executed program as a table with one row per line, putting each step's actual intermediate output beside its code line, so the reasoning trace is read as data rather than as boxes.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; the arXiv v1 PDF names no venue (remembered venue: CVPR 2023, unverified). Paradigm tagged 'Chain-of-Thought' as the closest listed prompting paradigm (LLM in-context generation of an intermediate program); VisProg is not in the paradigm list. Fig. 1 (narrow bottom-up generator -> interpreter strip beside five example panels) and Fig. 3 (prompt -> GPT-3 -> program) were judged quality 3; this card is the visual-rationale execution trace. The whole figure is one embedded raster (images_px covers the crop), so it was measured on fig4-drawn.png, a copy without the record; photo_share is null although much of it is photographs.

arrangement.units: two black-bordered example boxes stacked vertically; each holds a summary column and a ruled step table
arrangement.inputs_as: the instruction or statement as quoted text above real photographs (one image for editing, LEFT and RIGHT images for NLVR)

taxonomy.task: compositional visual reasoning and image editing by LLM-generated programs

insights.structure: Each example is a two-column table: the task and its input/prediction on the left, one ruled row per program step on the right.
insights.data: Every intermediate is drawn as the actual output (segmentation masks with labelled crops, a selected region, an edited photo, a count, 'True'), next to its syntax-coloured code line.
insights.emphasis: The step outputs themselves carry the figure; module names are bold red in the code and arguments in purple strings.
insights.flow: Steps read top to bottom, one per row, each with a short arrow from the code line to its output on the left.
insights.avoid: The left column repeats the input image and the final prediction at a larger size, duplicating the first and last rows of the table; the program-generation step (the LLM) is not in this figure.

core.what: one table row per executed program step, its intermediate output drawn as an image or value at the row's left beside the code line that made it

relations.form: program steps stacked top to bottom in ruled rows, each pairing an output thumbnail with its code line by a short arrow
intermediate operations drawn on the image itself: segmentation masks as black-ground labelled crops, the selected region boxed in green, edits shown as the edited photo
two task examples (image editing, NLVR) stacked as identical table layouts

channels.colour: code syntax only: bold red module names, blue variable names, purple string arguments; green boxes mark selected regions on the images
channels.shape: photos = data, monospace text = program; no module boxes
channels.line: short left arrows join each code line to its output; thin rules separate steps
channels.frame: a black border = one task example

quality.strengths: Every intermediate representation is drawn as data beside the step that made it, so the step-to-output relation is visible as one row each; arrows are short and straight; the code is syntax-coloured so module names stand out without boxes.
quality.weaknesses: The left summary column duplicates the first input and final output rows at a larger size; heavy table rules frame every row; the LLM that writes the program is absent, so the figure explains execution only.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
